title: Mechanisms regulating Meningeal Development and Function
text:
Metabolic waste accumulation due to meningeal disruption has been linked to the onset
of neurodegeneration, increased incidence of stroke, altered vascular permeability,
cognitive decline, and lower recovery from brain injury. Expanding our understanding of
the integral cell populations comprising the meninges and the pathways regulating their
development and function will help elucidate genetic mechanisms affecting meningeal
and CNS stability during disease.

title: Elucidating the contribution of lipid dysregulation to impaired oligodendrocyte maturation and myelination in Spinocerebellar ataxia type 3
text:
This proposal focuses on elucidating the mechanistic underpinnings of the early and progressive
oligodendrocyte maturation deficit in the neurodegenerative disease Spinocerebellar ataxia type 3 (SCA3).
Myelin is highly enriched for lipids, and my preliminary data establishes global lipid profile dysregulation in a
disease-vulnerable brain region of SCA3 mice and post-mortem patients, suggesting that lipid alterations may
play a role in the impairment of mature, myelinating oligodendrocytes in SCA3. In this proposal, I will
characterize myelin-specific lipid dysregulation in SCA3 mice and determine the necessity of mutant ATXN3 in
oligodendrocytes for cell-autonomous lipid dysregulation and impaired maturation, thus providing novel insight
into SCA3 pathogenesis and the mechanisms driving oligodendrocyte dysfunction.

title: Interdisciplinary Research Training in Pain and/or Substance Use Disorders
text:
Pain and substance use disorders (SUDs) are highly prevalent, commonly co-occurring and confer a
tremendous toll on society. There is an urgent need to train interdisciplinary researchers who can better
characterize these important conditions and translate discoveries to safe and effective treatments. The aim of
this postdoctoral training program is to develop the next generation of scientific leaders in pain and SUDs.

title: Identifying Upper Motor Neuron Pathology and Molecular Signatures in the Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS) Motor Cortex
text:
ALS, the most common motor neuron disease, is a neurodegenerative condition that results in progressive
weakness and ventilator-dependence or death within 3-4 years from onset and has no cure. The motor cortex
is known to play an important role but little is known about its pathophysiology. The proposed studies have the
potential to identify novel targets of upper motor neuron dysfunction for drug development, and could result in
the development of a non-invasive imaging biomarker for early identification of upper motor neuron dysfunction
and diagnosis.

title: Epigenetic mechanisms of sustained transcription across cocaine abstinence
text:
Cocaine use disorder is a chronic neuropsychiatric condition characterized by persistent craving during
abstinence that ultimately promotes relapse. The overall goal of this proposal is to define and therapeutically
target a putative abstinence-induced regulatory pathway, Nr4a1-CART, to promote recovery from cocaine use
disorder.

title: Molecular mechanism of INAFM2 in metastasis
text:
Metastasis is the major cause of mortality in cancer patients today, with over 90% of cancer deaths being due to
metastasis, and there are very few treatment options available for treating metastatic cancer. In my preliminary
work, I discovered a novel mediator of metastasis: the human INAFM2 protein, which may present a future
druggable target. The aims of this grant are to fully confirm INAFM2’s role in cancer metastasis by using mouse
models and to determine INAFM2’s biological function and molecular mechanism.

title: TRD2: Circular Ranging OCT
text: TRD-2 TRD project 2 will develop imaging platforms based on novel circular ranging (CR) architectures of optical coherence tomography. Specific Aim #1 addresses long-standing challenges to using OCT in open surgery. Conventional approaches burdened the surgeon with cumbersome equipment and required disruptions in workflow. We will leverage the depth-independence of CR to enable a head-mounted OCT microscope that can continuously survey the surgical field. This OCT loupe platform will be specifically developed to provide improved visualization of nerves to prevent accidental injury to these delicate and critical tissues, and thereby avoiding some of the most feared surgical morbidities. Specific Aim #2 integrates recent advancements in quantitative flow imaging with extremely rapid retinal CR-OCT technology to enable a platform for wide-field angiography and quantitative flow mapping in the human retina. Quantitative flow imaging will enable comprehensive, pulse resolved maps of the non-capillary retinal vascular networks, positioning investigators to decipher the interaction of retinal perfusion and disease. Wide-field angiography will reduce barriers that have limited clinicians and scientists from reliably and routinely imaging the peripheral retina Through these aims, TRD-2 will develop, validate, and deliver innovative technologies to our collaborating investigators and to the broader biomedical community.

title: Determinants of AAV Tropism
text:
The current proposal focuses on studying AAV capsid-genome interactions and the impact on transcription.
We will investigate how AAV structure regulates epigenetic signatures on the genome and controls
transcriptional activity of vector genomes across different species. Overall, we expect to develop a roadmap for
improving AAV vector design, thereby improving therapeutic efficacy and safety of AAV gene therapies.

title: Single Cell-Resolution Imaging of Drug Resistance via Toxic Metal Pre-exposure in Lung Patient Tumor Microenvironment
text:
Toxic metal pre-exposure can be an important but unexplored resistance mechanism for cancer therapy such
as platinum (Pt)-based therapy, particularly for toxic metal-polluted regions such as the US Appalachia. This
urgent and unmet need for improving patient care can be best addressed by developing a tool for in situ single
cell-resolution imaging of common toxic metals such as chromium (Cr)/lead (Pb) and Pt drug metal in
juxtaposition to tumor and drug resistance-promoting markers in the tumor microenvironment of Pt-resistant
patient tissues. A successful outcome will reveal a new drug resistance mechanism for cancer therapy that
contributes to Appalachian health disparity.

title: Medical Genetics Research Training Grant
text: We are in the midst of a medical revolution at the center of which is genetics and genomics. This period in medical history will likely be known as the “Genomics Era” and underscores the need for intensive and high quality human genetic research training of clinicians (M.D. and M.D., Ph.D.) trained in Pediatrics, Medicine, Psychiatry, Pathology and other specialties. This research training program seeks to provide this training primarily to a broad group of clinicians in all arenas relevant to human genetics and genomics. This training program will train future medical genetics leaders who are willing and able to apply modern research methods to elucidating the pathogenesis and pathophysiology of medical genetic conditions, as well as understanding how genetics and genomics will contribute to health maintenance through preventative care, so that new and more effective therapeutic interventions can be identified.

title: Molecular and Cellular Regulation of Vascular Calcification
text:
The abnormal deposition of bone-like mineral in the valve and vasculature, also known as
vascular calcification (VC), increases with age, vascular and valvular disease, diabetes
and chronic kidney disease (CKD). Calcification of these organs leads to loss of
compliance, stiffening and increased tendency to rupture, contributing to declining
cardiovascular function and heart failure. There are no drug therapies for VC. The
proposed research provides a foundation for future translational and clinical studies aimed
at identifying effective biomarkers and targets, as well as developing therapeutics to
prevent and/or treat VC.

title: Mechanisms of Perinatal Nicotine Vaping-Induced Pulmonary ILC2 Dysregulation and Allergic Asthma Development
text:
Asthma is a significant public health burden, affecting over 28 million people in the U.S., including a large
pediatric population, with current therapies targeting symptoms rather than underlying mechanisms. Smoking
during pregnancy and lactation is a major contributor to childhood asthma, and the sharp rise in electronic
cigarette use, particularly among pregnant women, has exacerbated the issue. Using advanced genetic and
molecular models, we aim to investigate how nicotine vaping during pregnancy and early development alters
pulmonary immune cells central to allergic responses and test a simple, clinically translatable approach to
mitigate perinatal nicotine exposure-induced asthma.

title: Understanding the Evolution, Biology, and Molecular Mechanism of Argonaute
text:
Argonaute proteins in animals, plants, yeasts, and bacteria use small pieces of RNA or DNA to
find and control genes. Studying how Argonautes work has already led to small RNA drugs to
turn off fatal human genes. The proposed research will reveal how organisms make small RNAs
and use Argonautes to control growth and reproductive health.

title: Strategies to improve therapy to pancreatic cancer with targeted-nanoparticle
text:
Pancreatic cancer will soon become the 2nd leading cause of cancer related deaths and has the poorest survival
of all solid tumors. In this project, we will study the ability of a biodegradable CCK-B receptor-targeted polyplex
nanoparticle to improve the efficacy of chemotherapy and immunotherapy. The nanoparticle has the potential to
be clinically relevant since it alters the barriers to treatment by decreasing fibrosis and reversing the
immunoresistance of the pancreatic tumor microenvironment.

title: Liquid biopsy cell-free DNA analysis to monitor sepsis
text:
This K08 Career Development Award Proposal describes the skills and further training that the PI, Dr. Nicholas
P. Semenkovich, M.D., Ph.D., will develop over the next five years to become an independent physician scientist
with unique expertise in sepsis and applications of liquid biopsy cell-free DNA as a predictive and prognostic
biomarker. Successful accomplishment of the proposed aims will establish a new paradigm for the study of
sepsis over its temporal presentation, including its catastrophic complications, and will define a new framework
for triage, management, and potential early intervention. Furthermore, the mentorship and training plan serve to
develop a candidate with expertise in basic science research and clinical acumen, a combination that is critically
important for future translational breakthroughs.

title: Analysis Core
text: ANALYSIS CORE SUMMARY There is extensive need for development of a skilled workforce for the study of disparities in Alzheimer’s Disease and Related Dementias (ADRD). Due to the aging of the US population, the numbers of people with ADRD are increasing, particularly among Latino and non-Latino Black compared with white individuals. The study of health disparities related to ADRD requires a transdisciplinary approach that includes research in the social and contextual factors, behavioral science, mental health, epidemiology, ADRD biomarkers, neuropsychology, measurement, biostatistics, bioinformatics, clinical trials, and caregiving. The Analysis Core (AnC) of the Columbia Center for Interdisciplinary Research on Alzheimer's Disease Disparities (CIRAD) has four main goals: 1) provide technical analytic support to RCMAR Scientists; 2) support a mentoring method for pilot investigators through study grids to be used in the Work-in-Progress (WIP) mentoring seminars, methods internships, and training workshops; 3) assist in the production and application of new measures and methods for studying health, social and environmental factors, and behavior across the life course; and 4) collaborate with investigators across RCMAR and other NIA-funded Centers. The AnC will leverage collaborations with the Columbia Alzheimer’s Disease Research Centers (ADRC), the Pepper Center at Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai, and the Weill Cornell Roybal Center to provide cross-site research and mentoring opportunities for RCMAR Scientists. The AnC will assist Research Education Component (REC) leaders (Drs. Byrd and Aiello) with applications from RCMAR Scientists. A focus of methodological development will be related to the primary theme of the CIRAD: interdisciplinary research on biological, behavioral, sociocultural, and environmental mechanisms of disparities in ADRD, including risk and resilience factors, biomarkers, caregiving, and analytic methods for secondary data analyses involving biomarkers. The proposed AnC focuses on measurement, but also examines analytic methods for secondary data analyses involving biomarkers. The AnC will achieve its goals through the following specific aims: Specific Aim 1: To support RCMAR Scientists through methodological and statistical mentoring; Specific Aim 2: To identify, catalog, distribute/disseminate informed measures; Specific Aim 3: To develop methods and analyses related to the CIRAD theme of mechanisms of ADRD disparities; Specific Aim 4: To develop new lines of investigation using existing and secondary data; and Specific Aim 5: To develop further collaborative relationships

title: Stigma and Recovery From Alcohol Use Disorder: A Mixed-Methods Analysis of Mindfulness Processes
text:
Disadvantaged communities experience disproportionate harms from alcohol use disorder (AUD) and face
heightened barriers to recovery. The proposed study will elucidate how mindfulness-based interventions foster
resilience to stigma and support recovery among these disadvantaged populations by integrating advanced
quantitative and qualitative methods to examine the complex interplay of stigma, mindfulness processes,
disadvantage, and recovery outcomes. Results will inform the development and optimization of contextually
sensitive, strengths-based, and mindfulness-based interventions for AUD that address stigma-related
challenges in AUD recovery, and enhance long-term recovery for disadvantaged individuals with AUD.

title: Translational Approach to Studying miRNA functions in sACC and amygdala in patients with BPD
text:
The goals of this application are: 1) identify miRNA differentially expressed in amygdala and
subgenual anterior cingulate cortex between subjects with BPD and matched neurotypical controls in a large
discovery and replication samples of BPD (N=300 and N=100, respectively); 2) uncover the genetic mechanisms
by which genome-wide significant polymorphisms from GWAS of BPD affect miRNA expression in these two
brain regions; 3) test the functional effect of a selected set of miRNA in mouse models to investigate BPD-like
behavioral measures.

title: A Predictive Framework for Human Infection Risk: Genomic Characterization of Vibrio spp. in the Context of Algal Blooms and Extreme Weather Events
text:
This research will improve understanding of how geophysical processes—such as sea surface temperature and
plankton dynamics—influence the presence and virulence of climate-sensitive Vibrio spp. in coastal waters. We
will develop an AI-enabled forecasting platform that integrates satellite remote sensing with pathogen genomics
to enable early detection and targeted public health responses. This work supports efforts to reduce the rising
burden of Vibrio-related illness and mortality in vulnerable coastal populations under extreme weather events
such as hurricane-induced flooding or harmful algal blooms in the Gulf of America.

title: Enabling Point of Care Diagnosis of Epilepsy in Underserved Populations
text:
Most of the 50 million people in the world with epilepsy lack access to basic diagnostic and treatment resources.
In this project, we will develop a comprehensive AI approach to detecting epileptiform discharges in EEG for
patients of all ages and epilepsy types; develop an easy-to-use risk score questionnaire that, in combination with
automated EEG interpretation, can allow non-experts to diagnose epilepsy as accurately as experts; and we will
field test this approach in an underserved area, Guinea West Africa, using a point-of-care EEG system. This
project will help reduce the epilepsy treatment gap by bringing accurate diagnostic services within reach of
patients suffering from epilepsy who live outside the reach of epilepsy experts.
